rules: The retained wealth settings are used unchanged for all 54 ownership paths; only matched revised physical assets and financial flows replace their source products. Historical results remain intact.

Revised and historical accounts use the same 0–220 annual boundary and checkpoints 0, 32, 100, 200 and 220. All amounts value the same U accounting convention in constant USD2041 equivalents, not nominal currency faces.

Worldwide services, commercial intellectual property, brands, software and unallocated service-package capital remain unvalued real assets. Geological potential and hypothetical accessible resource shares do not become permitted mining assets.

Programme reserve assets retain the matching restricted enterprise claim. Domestic deposits, loans, custody and equity have explicit counterparties; bank reserve money is not added to nonbank transaction money.

Ownership transfers allocate the same dated payouts. Community purchases pay the outside seller exactly; negotiated transfers are wealth transfers without additional output. New outside capital dilutes prior local stakes under the retained own-funds convention.

The source physical asset values are service-potential replacement-value proxies. A refurbished core enters the restored productive stock once; its restored service value is not a new cash receipt, production profit or market appraisal.

Distributed-cash return metrics exclude terminal claims. The separately labelled cash-plus-terminal comparison adds outside enterprise equity and outstanding outside custody once. Enterprise equity already includes net physical assets, work in progress, programme cash and restricted reserves less debt.

The residual foreign backing of assumed U balances is an accounting closure, not a solved balance of payments or independently available foreign currency. Neither revised savings nor the currency basket establish a currency-price or inflation forecast.
The accounting consumer does not qualify physical deployment, resource release, engineering recovery coefficients, markets or institutional ownership contracts.
